A rare genetic mutation called pseudo-melanism has resulted in roughly half of the tigers in India's Similipal Tiger Reserve sporting coats with far more black than those of usual tigers. This widespread coloration is a symptom of a shallow gene pool in a region that previously faced a dwindling tiger population, and could prove catastrophic if conservation officers aren't able to find these tigers more genetically diverse mates. A Tiger Is Not a TikTok Toy. A Young Man Is Dead. How many lives must be destroyed before humans understand that wild animals are not entertainment? In Pakistan, a 19-year-old caregiver lost his life after a captive big cat was brought out for a TikTok video. The influencer wanted fame. The animal wanted nothing to do with human fame. And a young man ended up dead. What breaks my heart is how casually humans treat wild animals as objects. Grab them. Push them. Force them to cooperate. Ignore their resistance. All for what? A few thousand likes? An animal cannot say NO in human language. But its body can scream NO. And when it does, why aren’t we listening? A wild animal can recognize its caregiver, trust him, and still attack when it feels threatened or restrained. That’s not betrayal. That’s instinct. The caregiver may have been following instructions. Perhaps years of familiarity made him believe he was safe. But shouldn’t anyone working with a powerful predator be trained to recognize when that animal has had enough? I feel sorrow for that young man. He paid with his life for a video that wasn’t even his. But I also feel sorrow for the animal. Humans created the situation. Humans ignored the danger. Yet somehow, the animal becomes the villain. A tiger doesn’t understand TikTok. It doesn’t understand followers, fame, or human stupidity. But humans understand consequences. Or at least we’re supposed to. The animal was reportedly taken into wildlife custody. Its fate should be determined by welfare and safety, not revenge. And the people who decided that a wild predator should perform for social media must answer for their decisions. The tiger didn’t betray anyone. Humans betrayed their responsibility to protect both the animal and the young man. Stop treating wild animals like toys. Their lives are worth more than your likes.
